questions.question: A block of wood is placed in a large tank of water. How can you tell if the whole block is floating?
options: If some part of the block is visible above the surface.
Only if the entire block is completely above the water surface.
If exactly half of the block is submerged under the water.
If the block sinks to the very bottom of the tank.

questions.question: A plastic toy floats perfectly in a shallow puddle of water. If you place the same toy into a deep swimming pool, what will happen to how well it floats?
options: It will float much higher because deep water has more upward pressure.
It will float in exactly the same way, because depth does not affect how well it floats.
It will sink to the bottom because deep water cannot support its weight.
It will float slightly lower because of the increased volume of water beneath it.

questions.question: Why can a heavy steel ship float on water, even though a solid block of steel sinks?
options: The steel used in ships is chemically treated to make it lighter than water.
The ship's engines constantly push it upwards to keep it afloat.
The ship's shape allows it to push aside a mass of water equal to its own mass before it goes under.
The air surrounding the ship pulls it upwards against the force of gravity.

questions.question: On Earth, approximately how much force is required to lift a bag of sugar with a mass of 1 kg?
options: 1 N

questions.question: In science, mass is often converted between grams and kilograms. How many grams are there in 1 kilogram?
A student adds equal weights to a spring and measures its extension. What pattern should they observe if the spring behaves normally?
options: The extension increases by the same amount for each equal increase in force.
The extension doubles with every single weight added, regardless of size.
The extension becomes smaller and smaller as more weights are added.
The extension changes randomly and has no predictable pattern.

questions.question: When we say the extension of a spring is 'directly proportional' to the force applied, what does this mean?
options: If you double the force, the extension is reduced by half.
If you double the force, the extension also doubles.
The extension remains constant no matter how much force is applied.
The force applied is always equal to the total length of the spring.

questions.question: Why is a metal spring described as being elastic?
options: It can be stretched to any length without ever breaking.
It returns to its original length once the stretching force is removed.
It permanently changes its shape when a small force is applied.
It generates its own thermal energy when it is compressed.

questions.question: What is one of the main mechanical advantages of using a lever?
options: It can multiply a small force into a larger force to move heavy objects.
It can completely eliminate the effect of gravity on an object.
It reduces the mass of the object being lifted.
It increases the total energy in a closed system.

questions.question: What is the main structural difference between the different types of levers?
options: The material from which the lever is constructed.
The position of the pivot relative to the load and effort.
The total length of the lever arm being used.
The amount of friction acting at the surface.

questions.question: In physics, what does pressure measure?
options: The total amount of mass in a given volume.
How concentrated a force is over a certain area.
The speed at which an object moves under a force.
The total energy stored inside a stretched spring.

questions.question: Which of the following formulas is used to calculate pressure?
options: Pressure = force × area
Pressure = area ÷ force
Pressure = force ÷ area
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is the standard unit of pressure that is equivalent to one newton per square metre?
options: The joule
The watt
The pascal (Pa)
The newton

questions.question: How does increasing the surface area of a boat's hull affect the potential upthrust acting on it?
options: It decreases the maximum upthrust because the boat becomes heavier.
It has no effect on upthrust because upthrust only depends on the depth of the water.
It allows for a bigger maximum upthrust because more water can be displaced.
It causes the upthrust to act in a horizontal direction instead of vertical.

questions.question: Why does a deep-sea diver experience greater pressure at the bottom of the ocean than near the surface?
options: The temperature of the water is much lower at the bottom.
There is more liquid above them pushing down due to gravity.
Saltwater is less dense at greater depths.
The water at the bottom moves at a much faster speed.

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as you climb up a high mountain?
options: The air temperature rises, causing molecules to move faster.
There is less air above you pushing down.
The Earth's gravity becomes significantly stronger at high altitudes.
Wind speeds are always higher at mountain peaks.

questions.question: If you add equal loads to a rubber band one by one, how does its extension compare to that of a standard metal spring?
options: Its extension increases by the exact same amount for each load, just like a spring.
Its extension increases by different amounts for each equal increase in force.
It does not extend at all until a massive force is suddenly applied.
Its extension is always directly proportional to the force applied.

questions.question: When a heavy object is placed in the middle of a wooden beam, what physical change is observed as the mass of the object increases?
options: The beam becomes shorter in length.
The beam bends more.
The beam becomes lighter.
The beam starts to rotate continuously.

questions.question: When you stand on a solid floor, your weight squashes the particles in the floor together. What is the result of this squashing?
options: The floor particles permanently deform and lose all their structure.
The floor particles exert a greater upward force to push back against your feet.
The floor particles stop vibrating entirely.
The floor particles pull your feet downward with an extra gravitational force.

questions.question: How do you calculate the turning effect (moment) of a force acting on a lever?
options: Moment = force + perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force ÷ perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = mass × acceleration from the pivot
